title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: vignette covers DALY burden estimation pipeline. repeat preprocessing — Preprocessing Workflow vignette. pipeline two stages: Resistance profile estimation — converts resistance prevalence data probability distributions 2^n binary resistance profiles (S/R per antibiotic class). Uses convex optimisation (GBD eq. 7.5.1.3). Burden calculation — applies relative-risk weights profiles computes YLL, YLD, total DALY burden. Input can come two sources:

title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: working pre-computed marginal resistance rates (e.g. GBD ST-GPR country estimates national surveillance summaries), supply directly tibble validate running QP.
code: marginals <- tibble::tibble(   pathogen         = rep(c("Klebsiella pneumoniae", "Escherichia coli"), each = 3),   antibiotic_class = rep(     c("Carbapenems", "3GC", "Fluoroquinolones"),     times = 2   ),   n_tested    = c(420L, 460L, 390L, 280L, 310L, 265L),   n_resistant = c(126L, 299L, 195L,  45L, 155L, 133L) ) %>%   dplyr::mutate(marginal_resistance = n_resistant / n_tested)  marginals #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   pathogen             antibiotic_class n_tested n_resistant marginal_resistance #>   <chr>                <chr>               <int>       <int>               <dbl> #> 1 Klebsiella pneumoni… Carbapenems           420         126               0.3   #> 2 Klebsiella pneumoni… 3GC                   460         299               0.65  #> 3 Klebsiella pneumoni… Fluoroquinolones      390         195               0.5   #> 4 Escherichia coli     Carbapenems           280          45               0.161 #> 5 Escherichia coli     3GC                   310         155               0.5   #> 6 Escherichia coli     Fluoroquinolones      265         133               0.502 validate_aggregate_inputs(   marginals,   pathogen_col    = "pathogen",   class_col       = "antibiotic_class",   rate_col        = "marginal_resistance",   n_tested_col    = "n_tested",   n_resistant_col = "n_resistant" )

title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: enumerate_binary_profiles() generates 2^n binary combinations given ordered class set. profile space QP optimises . row one resistance phenotype. SSS = pan-susceptible reference; RRR = pan-resistant. ordered classes vector defines bit positions must stay consistent throughout pipeline.
code: classes  <- c("Carbapenems", "3GC", "Fluoroquinolones") profiles <- enumerate_binary_profiles(classes) profiles #> # A tibble: 8 × 4 #>   profile_delta Carbapenems `3GC` Fluoroquinolones #>   <chr>               <int> <int>            <int> #> 1 SSS                     0     0                0 #> 2 RSS                     1     0                0 #> 3 SRS                     0     1                0 #> 4 RRS                     1     1                0 #> 5 SSR                     0     0                1 #> 6 RSR                     1     0                1 #> 7 SRR                     0     1                1 #> 8 RRR                     1     1                1

title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: build_constraint_matrix() constructs constraint matrix M target vector v encode marginal pairwise constraints fed QP. Marginal rows M: entry = 1 class resistant profile. Pairwise rows: entry = 1 classes pair resistant.
code: kp      <- marginals[marginals$pathogen == "Klebsiella pneumoniae", ] r_marg  <- setNames(kp$marginal_resistance, kp$antibiotic_class) profiles_enum <- enumerate_binary_profiles(names(r_marg)) cm      <- build_constraint_matrix(profiles_enum, r_marg)  cat("M dimension (constraints x profiles):", dim(cm$M), "\n") #> M dimension (constraints x profiles): 6 8 cat("Constraint targets (marginals + pairwise independence fallback):\n") #> Constraint targets (marginals + pairwise independence fallback): round(cm$v, 4) #>      Carbapenems              3GC Fluoroquinolones                   #>            0.300            0.650            0.500            0.195  #>                                    #>            0.150            0.325

title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: estimate_profiles_convex() runs full pipeline pathogens one call: validates, enumerates, builds constraints, solves QP. solver prefers osqp (sparse, fast) quadprog fallback. profile_class_set column records exact ordered class set defines binary code — must carried forward downstream DALY attribution prevent class-order ambiguity.
code: panel_map <- list(   "Klebsiella pneumoniae"  = c("Carbapenems",                                 "3GC",                                 "Fluoroquinolones"),   "Escherichia coli"       = c("Carbapenems",                                 "3GC",                                 "Fluoroquinolones") )  profiles_out <- estimate_profiles_convex(   marginals    = marginals,   pairwise     = NULL,   panel_map    = panel_map,   lambda       = 1e-8,   pathogen_col = "pathogen",   class_col    = "antibiotic_class",   rate_col     = "marginal_resistance",   n_tested_col = "n_tested" ) profiles_out %>%   dplyr::select(pathogen, profile_delta, profile_probability,                 convergence_flag, max_abs_residual) %>%   dplyr::filter(profile_probability > 0.005) %>%   dplyr::arrange(pathogen, dplyr::desc(profile_probability)) #> # A tibble: 16 × 5 #>    pathogen  profile_delta profile_probability convergence_flag max_abs_residual #>    <chr>     <chr>                       <dbl> <lgl>                       <dbl> #>  1 Escheric… SSS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  2 Escheric… RSS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  3 Escheric… SRS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  4 Escheric… RRS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  5 Escheric… SSR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  6 Escheric… RSR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  7 Escheric… SRR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  8 Escheric… RRR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.339 #>  9 Klebsiel… SSS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2   #> 10 Klebsiel… RSS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2   #> 11 Klebsiel… SRS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2   #> 12 Klebsiel… RRS                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2   #> 13 Klebsiel… SSR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2   #> 14 Klebsiel… RSR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2   #> 15 Klebsiel… SRR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2   #> 16 Klebsiel… RRR                         0.125 FALSE                       0.2 profiles_out %>%   dplyr::distinct(pathogen, profile_class_set, estimator) #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   pathogen              profile_class_set                estimator #>   <chr>                 <chr>                            <chr>     #> 1 Klebsiella pneumoniae 3GC|Carbapenems|Fluoroquinolones convex    #> 2 Escherichia coli      3GC|Carbapenems|Fluoroquinolones convex

title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: working isolate-level AST data (preprocessing), use three-step pipeline feeds QP engine.
code: set.seed(101) # Minimal long-format AST data: one row per isolate x antibiotic class ast_class <- data.frame(   isolate_id       = rep(paste0("ISO", sprintf("%03d", 1:80)), each = 3),   organism_name    = rep(     ifelse(seq_len(80) <= 50, "Klebsiella pneumoniae", "Escherichia coli"),     each = 3   ),   org_group        = "Enterobacterales",   antibiotic_class = rep(c("Carbapenems", "3GC", "Fluoroquinolones"), times = 80),   antibiotic_value = sample(     c("S", "R"), 240, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.60, 0.40)   ),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) # Step 1 -- marginal resistance per pathogen x class marg_out <- compute_marginal_resistance(   ast_class,   pathogen_col         = "organism_name",   org_group_col        = "org_group",   isolate_col          = "isolate_id",   antibiotic_class_col = "antibiotic_class",   antibiotic_value_col = "antibiotic_value",   min_n_tested         = 10L )  marg_out$marginal #> # A tibble: 6 × 6 #>   organism_name         org_group        antibiotic_class n_tested n_resistant #>   <chr>                 <chr>            <chr>               <int>       <int> #> 1 Escherichia coli      Enterobacterales Fluoroquinolones       30          14 #> 2 Escherichia coli      Enterobacterales 3GC                    30          12 #> 3 Escherichia coli      Enterobacterales Carbapenems            30          10 #> 4 Klebsiella pneumoniae Enterobacterales Fluoroquinolones       50          27 #> 5 Klebsiella pneumoniae Enterobacterales 3GC                    50          21 #> 6 Klebsiella pneumoniae Enterobacterales Carbapenems            50          17 #> # ℹ 1 more variable: marginal_resistance <dbl> # Step 2 -- pairwise co-resistance matrices per pathogen co_out <- compute_pairwise_coresistance(   marg_out,   pathogen_col         = "organism_name",   isolate_col          = "isolate_id",   antibiotic_class_col = "antibiotic_class",   min_co_tested        = 5L )  round(co_out[["Klebsiella pneumoniae"]]$prevalence, 3) #>                   3GC Carbapenems Fluoroquinolones #> 3GC                NA        0.18             0.24 #> Carbapenems      0.18          NA             0.16 #> Fluoroquinolones 0.24        0.16               NA # Step 3 -- profile probabilities via QP rp_out <- compute_resistance_profiles(   marg_out,   co_out,   pathogen_col         = "organism_name",   antibiotic_class_col = "antibiotic_class",   exclude_near_zero    = FALSE )  rp_out[["Klebsiella pneumoniae"]]$profiles %>%   dplyr::filter(probability > 0.005) %>%   dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(probability)) #>   profile probability 3GC Carbapenems Fluoroquinolones #> 1     SSS       0.125   0           0                0 #> 2     RSS       0.125   1           0                0 #> 3     SRS       0.125   0           1                0 #> 4     RRS       0.125   1           1                0 #> 5     SSR       0.125   0           0                1 #> 6     RSR       0.125   1           0                1 #> 7     SRR       0.125   0           1                1 #> 8     RRR       0.125   1           1                1 # Constraint residuals: how well does the solution reproduce the inputs? round(rp_out[["Klebsiella pneumoniae"]]$constraint_residuals, 6) #>                          marg_3GC                  marg_Carbapenems  #>                              0.08                              0.16  #>             marg_Fluoroquinolones              pair_3GC_Carbapenems  #>                             -0.04                              0.07  #>         pair_3GC_Fluoroquinolones pair_Carbapenems_Fluoroquinolones  #>                              0.01                              0.09

title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: check_profile_constraints() formally verifies estimated probabilities satisfy non-negativity, sum--one, reproduce input marginal rates within tolerance. accepts named-list format compute_resistance_profiles() directly.
code: checks <- check_profile_constraints(   rp_out,   marginals    = marg_out$marginal,   tolerance    = 1e-3,   pathogen_col = "organism_name",   class_col    = "antibiotic_class",   rate_col     = "marginal_resistance" )  checks %>%   dplyr::select(pathogen, constraint_type, constraint_name,                 target, reconstructed, abs_residual, pass) #> # A tibble: 22 × 7 #>    pathogen    constraint_type constraint_name target reconstructed abs_residual #>    <chr>       <chr>           <chr>            <dbl>         <dbl>        <dbl> #>  1 Escherichi… nonneg          min_probability NA             0.125      NA      #>  2 Escherichi… sum_to_one      sum_probability  1             1           0      #>  3 Escherichi… marginal        marg_3GC         0.4           0.5         0.1    #>  4 Escherichi… marginal        marg_Carbapene…  0.333         0.5         0.167  #>  5 Escherichi… marginal        marg_Fluoroqui…  0.467         0.5         0.0333 #>  6 Escherichi… pairwise        pair_3GC_Carba…  0.167         0.25        0.0833 #>  7 Escherichi… pairwise        pair_3GC_Fluor…  0.133         0.25        0.117  #>  8 Escherichi… pairwise        pair_Carbapene…  0.2           0.25        0.05   #>  9 Escherichi… marginal        marg_Fluoroqui…  0.467         0.5         0.0333 #> 10 Escherichi… marginal        marg_3GC         0.4           0.5         0.1    #> # ℹ 12 more rows #> # ℹ 1 more variable: pass <lgl>

title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: bootstrap_profiles_convex() resamples resistant counts Binomial distribution refits QP B times, returning percentile confidence intervals profile probability.
code: boot <- bootstrap_profiles_convex(   marginals       = marginals,   B               = 300L,   seed            = 42L,   alpha           = 0.05,   pathogen_col    = "pathogen",   class_col       = "antibiotic_class",   n_tested_col    = "n_tested",   n_resistant_col = "n_resistant" )  boot[["Klebsiella pneumoniae"]] %>%   dplyr::filter(probability_mean > 0.005) %>%   dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(probability_mean)) #> # A tibble: 0 × 7 #> # ℹ 7 variables: profile <chr>, probability_mean <dbl>, #> #   probability_median <dbl>, lower <dbl>, upper <dbl>, #> #   n_replicates_converged <int>, convergence_rate <dbl>

what: Stage 2 — Assigning Relative Risk to Profiles
title: DALY Burden Estimation Workflow in anumaan
text: daly_assign_rr_to_profiles() applies GBD max rule: profile-level LOS relative risk maximum RR across resistant classes profile.
code: # Synthetic LOS relative risk estimates (from daly_fit_los_rr() in practice) # pathogen column must match the keys in rp_out (organism_name column values) rr_table <- tibble::tibble(   organism_name    = rep(c("Klebsiella pneumoniae", "Escherichia coli"), each = 3),   antibiotic_class = rep(c("Carbapenems", "3GC", "Fluoroquinolones"), times = 2),   RR_LOS    = c(2.1, 1.6, 1.4,  1.8, 1.5, 1.3),   CI_lower  = c(1.7, 1.3, 1.1,  1.4, 1.2, 1.0),   CI_upper  = c(2.6, 2.0, 1.8,  2.3, 1.9, 1.7) )  rr_table #> # A tibble: 6 × 5 #>   organism_name         antibiotic_class RR_LOS CI_lower CI_upper #>   <chr>                 <chr>             <dbl>    <dbl>    <dbl> #> 1 Klebsiella pneumoniae Carbapenems         2.1      1.7      2.6 #> 2 Klebsiella pneumoniae 3GC                 1.6      1.3      2   #> 3 Klebsiella pneumoniae Fluoroquinolones    1.4      1.1      1.8 #> 4 Escherichia coli      Carbapenems         1.8      1.4      2.3 #> 5 Escherichia coli      3GC                 1.5      1.2      1.9 #> 6 Escherichia coli      Fluoroquinolones    1.3      1        1.7 profiles_rr <- daly_assign_rr_to_profiles(   profiles_output = rp_out,   rr_table        = rr_table,   pathogen_col    = "organism_name",   class_col       = "antibiotic_class",   rr_col          = "RR_LOS",   fallback_rr     = 1 )  profiles_rr[["Klebsiella pneumoniae"]] %>%   dplyr::select(profile, probability, RR_LOS_profile, dominant_class) %>%   dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(probability)) #>   profile probability RR_LOS_profile   dominant_class #> 1     SSS       0.125            1.0  all_susceptible #> 2     RSS       0.125            1.6              3GC #> 3     SRS       0.125            2.1      Carbapenems #> 4     RRS       0.125            2.1      Carbapenems #> 5     SSR       0.125            1.4 Fluoroquinolones #> 6     RSR       0.125            1.6              3GC #> 7     SRR       0.125            2.1      Carbapenems #> 8     RRR       0.125            2.1      Carbapenems

title: Getting Started with anumaan
text: anumaan R package preprocessing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) surveillance data estimating disease burden using GBD methodology. structured around two sequential, independent pipelines can used together separately.

title: Getting Started with anumaan
text: Vignette: Preprocessing Workflow preprocessing pipeline standardises raw hospital surveillance data analysis-ready format. covers: Column name standardisation schema alignment Date parsing chronological validation Organism, specimen, antibiotic, AST value cleaning Demographic derivations (age, HAI/CAI, LOS) Event creation, deduplication, readmission classification Contaminant detection polymicrobial weighting Attrition tracking analysis-readiness filtering functions start prep_. pipeline entry point run_preprocess() automated runs modular prep_* functions staged, inspectable workflows. See full step--step walkthrough Preprocessing Workflow vignette.
code: library(anumaan)  # Full automated pipeline result <- run_preprocess(   data   = your_ast_data,   config = amr_config(hai_cutoff = 3, event_gap_days = 14) )  # Or modular data <- prep_standardize_organisms(data, organism_col = "organism_name") data <- prep_harmonize_ast(data, ast_col = "antibiotic_value") data <- prep_create_event_ids(data, patient_col = "patient_id",                                date_col = "date_of_culture")

title: Getting Started with anumaan
text: Vignette: DALY Burden Estimation DALY pipeline takes analysis-ready preprocessed data produces resistance-profile probability distributions GBD-style burden estimates. covers: Resistance profile estimation via convex optimisation (Pathway 1) — works either facility line-list data pre-computed aggregate marginals (GBD ST-GPR, GLASS, national surveillance networks) Marginal pairwise co-resistance computation Pearson back-calculation Profile probability estimation solving simplex-constrained QP Bootstrap uncertainty intervals profile probabilities Years Life Lost (YLL) — associated attributable Years Lived Disability (YLD) — associated attributable Total DALY burden per pathogen, hospital, organism group estimation functions start daly_. Profile-specific functions compute_*, estimate_*, enumerate_*, build_*, validate_*, check_*, bootstrap_*. See full walkthrough DALY Burden Estimation vignette.
code: # From aggregate marginals (GBD / GLASS / national surveillance) profiles <- estimate_profiles_convex(   marginals = your_marginals_table,   panel_map = list(     "Klebsiella pneumoniae" = c("Carbapenems", "3GC", "Fluoroquinolones")   ) )  # Assign LOS relative risk and compute fatal resistance prevalence profiles_rr <- daly_assign_rr_to_profiles(profiles, rr_table) R_k         <- daly_calc_resistance_prevalence_fatal(profiles_rr)

title: Preprocessing Workflow in anumaan
text: prep_deduplicate_ast() runs two sequential steps: Exact-duplicate removal — drops rows fully identical across patient, organism, antibiotic, date, value. true redundant records (e.g. result entered twice) ambiguity. Conflict resolution — exact duplicates gone, detects groups patient + organism + antibiotic + date different values (e.g. one lab returns S, another returns R), flags resolves via strategy. Step 1 — exact duplicates removed automatically: Step 2 — conflict detection exact-dedup:
code: ast_exact_dups <- data.frame(   patient_id            = c("pt_030", "pt_030", "pt_031"),   culture_date          = as.Date(c("2025-02-01", "2025-02-01", "2025-02-01")),   organism_normalized   = c("escherichia coli", "escherichia coli", "klebsiella pneumoniae"),   antibiotic_normalized = c("amikacin", "amikacin", "ciprofloxacin"),   ast_value_harmonized  = c("R", "R", "S"),   stringsAsFactors      = FALSE )  # 3 rows in — rows 1 and 2 are identical on all 5 key columns # step 1 removes the duplicate → 2 rows out, no conflicts flagged out_exact <- prep_deduplicate_ast(ast_exact_dups, mode = "detect") nrow(out_exact) #> [1] 2 out_exact[, c("patient_id", "antibiotic_normalized", "ast_value_harmonized", "is_ast_duplicate")] #>   patient_id antibiotic_normalized ast_value_harmonized is_ast_duplicate #> 1     pt_030              amikacin                    R            FALSE #> 2     pt_031         ciprofloxacin                    S            FALSE ast_dups <- data.frame(   patient_id            = c("pt_020", "pt_020", "pt_020"),   culture_date          = as.Date(c("2025-01-15", "2025-01-15", "2025-01-15")),   organism_normalized   = c("escherichia coli", "escherichia coli", "escherichia coli"),   antibiotic_normalized = c("amikacin", "amikacin", "cefotaxime"),   antibiotic_name       = c("Amikacin", "Amikacin", "Cefotaxime"),   antibiotic_class      = c("Aminoglycosides", "Aminoglycosides", "Third-generation-cephalosporins"),   antibiotic_value      = c("S", "R", "I"),   ast_value_harmonized  = c("S", "R", "I"),   stringsAsFactors      = FALSE )  # detect mode: inspect which rows are flagged as conflicting prep_deduplicate_ast(ast_dups, mode = "detect")[, c(   "patient_id",   "antibiotic_normalized",   "ast_value_harmonized",   "is_ast_duplicate" )] #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   patient_id organism_normalized antibiotic_normalized culture_date #>   <chr>      <chr>               <chr>                 <date>       #> 1 pt_020     escherichia coli    amikacin              2025-01-15   #> # ℹ 2 more variables: conflicting_values <chr>, n_rows <int> #>   patient_id antibiotic_normalized ast_value_harmonized is_ast_duplicate #> 1     pt_020              amikacin                    S             TRUE #> 2     pt_020              amikacin                    R             TRUE #> 3     pt_020            cefotaxime                    I            FALSE  # remove mode: resolve conflicts in one call — resistant_wins keeps "R" prep_deduplicate_ast(ast_dups, mode = "remove", strategy = "resistant_wins")[, c(   "patient_id",   "antibiotic_normalized",   "ast_value_harmonized" )] #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   patient_id organism_normalized antibiotic_normalized culture_date #>   <chr>      <chr>               <chr>                 <date>       #> 1 pt_020     escherichia coli    amikacin              2025-01-15   #> # ℹ 2 more variables: conflicting_values <chr>, n_rows <int> #> # A tibble: 2 × 3 #>   patient_id antibiotic_normalized ast_value_harmonized #>   <chr>      <chr>                 <chr>                #> 1 pt_020     amikacin              R                    #> 2 pt_020     cefotaxime            I

title: Bootstrap Uncertainty Intervals for Resistance Profile Probabilities — bootstrap_profiles_convex
text: marginals Data frame. Marginal resistance rates minimum columns pathogen_col, class_col, n_tested_col, n_resistant_col. $marginal element compute_marginal_resistance(), flat tibble structure compute_marginals_from_data(). coresistance_output Named list NULL. Output compute_pairwise_coresistance() (one entry per pathogen $T_matrix, $R_matrix, $prevalence). supplied, pairwise co-resistance resampled per replicate. NULL, independence fallback \(P(\cap B) = P() P(B)\) used every replicate. Default NULL. B Integer. Number bootstrap replicates. Default 500. seed Integer. Random seed reproducibility. Default 123. alpha Numeric. Two-sided interval width. Default 0.05 (.e., 95% intervals). n_cores Integer. Parallel cores via parallel::mclapply. Default 1L. exclude_near_zero Logical. Passed compute_resistance_profiles(). Default TRUE. top_n_classes Integer NULL. Cap number classes per pathogen. Default NULL. sigma_sq Numeric. QP constraint variance. Default 1. ridge Numeric. QP Hessian ridge term. Default 1e-8. pathogen_col Character. Pathogen column marginals. Default "organism_name". class_col Character. Class column marginals. Default "antibiotic_class". n_tested_col Character. Tested-count column. Default "n_tested". n_resistant_col Character. Resistant-count column. Default "n_resistant". org_group_col Character. Organism-group column (passed QP engine). Default "org_group".

title: Bootstrap Uncertainty Intervals for Resistance Profile Probabilities — bootstrap_profiles_convex
text: named list, one entry per pathogen. entry tibble   columns: profile Profile label (e.g. "RSS"). probability_mean Mean profile probability across B replicates. probability_median Median across replicates. lower Lower percentile (alpha / 2). upper Upper percentile (1 - alpha / 2). n_replicates_converged Number replicates     QP converged (non-uniform solution). convergence_rate Proportion replicates converged. point-estimate profiles tibble (single run original marginals) stored attribute "point_estimate".

title: Bootstrap Uncertainty Intervals for Resistance Profile Probabilities — bootstrap_profiles_convex
text: Resampling mechanism: bootstrap replicate \(b\) (pathogen, class) cell: $$n_{\text{resistant}}^{(b)} \sim \text{Binomial}(n_{\text{tested}},\; \hat{r}_{kd})$$ bootstrap marginal \(\hat{r}_{kd}^{(b)} = n_{\text{resistant}}^{(b)} / n_{\text{tested}}\). Pairwise co-resistance rates (supplied) resampled analogously. QP re-solved bootstrap marginal using existing compute_resistance_profiles() engine. Performance: \(n \leq 12\) classes QP solves milliseconds; B = 500 replicates complete seconds. \(n \geq 14\) classes use n_cores > 1 reduce B.

title: Bootstrap Uncertainty Intervals for Resistance Profile Probabilities — bootstrap_profiles_convex

text: $$\min_p \|Mp - v\|^2_W \quad \text{s.t.} \quad p \ge 0,\; \sum p = 1$$ Marginal rows: \(M_{d,\delta} = 1\) iff class \(d\) resistant profile \(\delta\). Pairwise rows: \(M_{d_1 d_2,\delta} = 1\) iff classes resistant. pairwise value unavailable (co-tested isolates), product marginals (independence assumption) substituted. Pairwise values exceed \(\min(P(), P(B))\) capped.

text: Named list, one entry per pathogen, list : profiles Data frame: profile (character label,     e.g.\ "RSR"), probability (\(\hat{p}_\delta\)),     one binary (0/1) integer column per antibiotic class indicating whether     class resistant (1) susceptible (0)     profile. classes Character vector antibiotic class names used     (alphabetical; bit 0 = classes[1]). n_classes Integer. Number classes used. constraint_residuals Named numeric vector     \(m_i^\top \hat{p} - v_i\) constraint. Small absolute     values indicate good constraint satisfaction.

title: Compute Resistance Profile Probabilities per Pathogen — compute_resistance_profiles
text: $$   \hat{p} = \arg\min_{p \\Delta_{2^n}}             \sum_{=1}^{m} \frac{(m_i^\top p - v_i)^2}{\sigma_i^2} $$ \(m = n(n+1)/2\) data-derived linear constraints encode n marginal resistance rates n(n-1)/2 pairwise co-resistance rates, \(\Delta\) standard probability simplex. QP solved via quadprog::solve.QP. small ridge term (ridge) added Hessian guarantee strict positive-definiteness. solver failure pathogen gets uniform distribution profiles.

title: Compute Resistance Profile Probabilities per Pathogen — compute_resistance_profiles
text: Marginal (rows 1 n) Row \(d\): \(M_{d,\delta} = 1\) iff \(\delta_d = 1\)       (.e., class \(d\) resistant profile \(\delta\)).       Constraint: \(\sum_\delta M_{d,\delta}\,p_\delta = \hat{r}_{kd}\). Pairwise (rows n+1 m) Row \((d_1,d_2)\): \(M_{d_1 d_2,\delta} = 1\) iff       \(\delta_{d_1} = 1 \land \delta_{d_2} = 1\).       Constraint: \(\sum_\delta M_{d_1 d_2,\delta}\,p_\delta =       \hat{r}_{k,d_1 d_2}\).       pairwise estimate unavailable (co-tested isolates),       product marginals (independence assumption) used fallback.

Overall mortality PAF pathogen k: $$\text{PAF}_{k,\text{mort}} = \sum_\delta \text{PAF}_{kd,\text{mort}}   = \frac{\sum_\delta R'_{K\delta}(\text{}_{K\delta}-1)}          {1 + \sum_\delta R'_{K\delta}(\text{}_{K\delta}-1)}$$ Usage pipeline:

Assign OR to profiles via max rule (rr_col = "OR_death")   profiles_with_or <- assign_rr_to_profiles(       profiles_output,       rr_table = mort_or,       rr_col   = "OR_death"   )    # 3. text: event_class_data Data frame. One row per organism-event. Antibiotic class columns hold 0 (susceptible), 1 (resistant), NA (tested). Metadata columns hold covariates grouping variables. class_cols Character vector. Names antibiotic class columns. Required. fixed_effects Character vector. Event-level covariate column names. Required. random_effects Character vector length 1, 2, 3. Grouping column names. First element: hospital (upper); second (optional): patient; third (optional): admission. Required. pathogen Character NULL. supplied, filters event_class_data rows pathogen_col equals value fitting. Recommended: fit one pathogen time. pathogen_col Character. Column identifying pathogen. Default "pathogen". event_id_col Character. Column event_class_data holding unique event identifiers. Default "event_id". eligible_pairs Tibble NULL. Hospital x pathogen pairs include. NULL uses pairs present data. outcome_col Character NULL. Patient outcome column. used downstream split R_ALL R_NF cohorts – enter probit likelihood. Default NULL. reserve_drug_cols Character vector NULL. Class columns exclude main model. panel_eligibility Named list. Eligibility thresholds per hospital x class cell: min_tested (default 30), min_resistant (default 5), min_susceptible (default 5). Cells meeting thresholds reported fitting still proceeds. residual_structure Character. Controls residual covariance structure. "identity" (default): classes conditionally independent given fixed random effects – residual covariance = I_D. "correlated": estimates full residual correlation matrix \(\Omega\) via LKJCholesky prior. Use "correlated" panel co-testing overlap adequate (check $eligibility_report$pairwise); otherwise \(\Omega\) driven mainly LKJ prior adds identifiability risk. estimand Character. Identifies target quantity. "observed_stewardship_event_mix" currently supported. prior_config Named list. subset beta_sd (default 1.5), tau_sd (default 1.0), lkj_eta (default 2.0). sampler_config Named list. Sampler settings forwarded cmdstanr::sample(): chains (4), iter_warmup (1000), iter_sampling (1000), adapt_delta (NULL, uses Stan default), max_treedepth (NULL), seed (123), parallel_chains (NULL), max_param_count (NULL – set positive integer stop approximate parameter count exceeds threshold). additional entries forwarded via .... show_messages Logical. title: Fit Bayesian Hierarchical Multivariate Probit Model for Resistance Profiles — fit_bayesian_multivariate_probit
text: Model (per pathogen): $$Y_{ed} = \mathbf{1}(Z_{ed} > 0)$$ $$Z_{ed} = \mathbf{x}_e^\top\beta_d   + \text{hospital\_effect}_{d,h(e)}   \;[+\; \text{patient\_effect}_{d,p(e)}]   \;[+\; \text{admission\_effect}_{d,(e)}]   + (L_\Omega\,\eta_e)_d$$ $$\eta_e \sim N(0, I_D),\quad L_\Omega \sim \text{LKJCholesky}(\eta)$$ per-event latent noise \(\eta_e\) makes \(L_\Omega\) (therefore \(\Omega = L_\Omega L_\Omega^\top\)) identifiable observed binary outcomes. Hospital (lower-level) effects use \(\text{diag}(\tau) L_{\text{corr}} z_{\text{raw}}\) parameterisation D-dim random effect vectors correlated across antibiotic classes. Single-pathogen design: pass pathogen restrict fit. Run per pathogen orchestrate analysis repository. Random effects (random_effects): 1, 2, 3 grouping column names defining clustering hierarchy (e.g. hospital; hospital + patient; hospital + patient + admission). first element upper-level; subsequent elements nested within . Nested levels receive globally unique composite keys built internally. hierarchical grouping variable can occupy slot – labels hospital/patient/admission semantic conventions, constraints. Isolate- sample-event-level effects can passed second third element, note returned object uses generic level names (upper_re_col, middle_re_col, lower_re_col). Missing-AST handling: Observed AST cells impose sign constraints latent variables; untested cells impose sign constraint represented unconstrained latent values. model assumes testing conditionally ignorable given included covariates random effects. correct selective testing bias. See residual_structure control residual covariance complexity. Fixed-effect missingness: function warns silently impute covariates. Imputation caller's responsibility; columns remaining NA values call cause Stan fail.

title: Preprocess AST Data for Resistance Profile Estimation (Pathway 1) — preprocess_for_profiles
text: Pipeline steps (order): Input validation via validate_profile_inputs(). Wide -> long conversion wide format detected     (prep_pivot_ast_wide_to_long()). AST value harmonisation – clean messy strings, resolve values     (prep_harmonize_ast()). Antibiotic name standardisation class column     (prep_standardize_antibiotics()). Class assignment still absent     (prep_classify_antibiotic_class()). Class-level collapse: R class => class = R     (prep_collapse_class_level()). Counting unit isolate_id. Year derivation date_col "year"     stratify_by. Organism-specific panel filter: retain user-specified classes     per pathogen. Long -> wide pivot antibiotic-class columns     (prep_create_wide_ast_matrix()). Counting unit: statistics computed per unique isolate_id. patient multiple isolates contributes one count per isolate, one count per patient.
